headline: It’s been an interesting 48 hours.

Introducing 𝚡𝚎𝚎𝚝: https://t.co/YaLEMbmKwf. A hermetic, pixel-perfect X post renderer in safe Rust / wasm. Zero browser, network, filesystem, system fonts. Renders a post to PNG in ~1ms (and 0.4 ms for @jack's "setting up my twttr" 😁). X is the global town square, and the medium is the message. Being able to preview what things will look like before posting is great for both humans and agents. Rendering with xeet is is 100x-1000x faster than booting up a browser and taking a screenshot, yet it's just as accurate. It reproduces Blink & HarfBuzz text shaping, 1/64px line breaking, RTL bidi, 28 Chirp font subsets, CJK/Math/Emoji fallbacks, "Show more" rules, etc. It's the kind of thing that would be wildly impractical, if not impossible, for a human engineer to pull off. Except 𝚡𝚎𝚎𝚝 is structured as an "autorepo." An oracle boots up Chrome, and verifies tens of thousands of text layout rules. A CI canary then watches the evolution of the original, and files signed PRs for agents to act on. It was conceived from the ground up around 'verification engineering', and the result speaks for itself. Enjoy!

"Do you find being a designer more fun now that you can easily prototype everything?" That's the question I asked @nateparrott (Anthropic). His answer: "I'm a little weird in that I have an engineering background. Before Anthropic, I worked at The Browser Company, where we made a browser called Arc. We spent a year in pre-production before we released Arc. It took us a couple weeks to build out each idea and see which worked. Now at Anthropic, you can kind of do that in one to two days. So you've really compressed the cycle of building. What you haven't compressed is the cycle of putting it in people's hands and understanding if they're going to use it." 📌 Watch our full episode here: https://t.co/HPX5HjXafX
